name: Optogenetics: Controlling Brain Cells with Light
description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to researchers Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their work on optogenetics. Optogenetics is the technique of using genetically expressed light-sensitive  proteins to control the activity of brain cells. 

Join Upinder Singh Bhalla for a lecture tracing the story of how very basic research into the light responsiveness of a single-celled plant micro-organism led to the discovery of light-sensitive proteins that allow current to flow into a cell. Learn how this was then developed into a powerful tool for studying the brain, and possibly for therapeutic purposes in the future. Come discover the path of development of optogenetics, both as a triumph of basic science, and also as a way to tell the story of many people who contributed fundamentally but were left aside when the prizes rolled in.

This lecture is organised in collaboration with Infosys Science Foundation.

name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Mediators, Manasi and Srivikashini, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: The Playful Writer: What Anne Carson Taught Me
description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature went to Anne Carson. 

Join Srilata Krishnan for a talk about Carson’s work and what writers and artists can learn from it. Carson’s training was in the classics, which spurred in her a wide-ranging interest in comparative literature, anthropology, history and the arts. Hers is a quintessentially interdisciplinary mind, and her work feels like jewels studded with the gemstones of ancient Greek and Latin literature (Sappho, Catullus, Stesichorus, for instance) and of writers such as Virginia Woolf, Keats and Gertrude Stein.

Formally, her work may be best described as cross-genre. It is the spirit of playfulness and enquiry that drives all of Carson’s work, making each of her books different from the others. Her playfulness precludes neither depth nor rigour, as borne out by every single work of hers. 

As a writer, Srilata has learnt a lot about craft from Carson and will be sharing the subtle ways in which reading Carson helped shape her own writing.

This lecture is organised in collaboration with Infosys Science Foundation.

name: Hello, Quantum!
description:
Ready to write your first program for a quantum computer?

Join us for an interactive session exploring one of the most exciting frontiers in modern technology—quantum computing. Discover what makes quantum computers different from the devices we use every day, and get acquainted with the fascinating world of qubits, superposition and quantum circuits. 

With Qiskit, an open-source software framework for quantum computing, we’ll go beyond theory to see how quantum programs actually work and take our first steps towards writing one ourselves. No prior knowledge of quantum computing is required—just curiosity and a willingness to experiment! Whether you’re a student, a technology enthusiast or simply curious about the quantum world, come along to demystify the science, explore new possibilities and experience quantum computing hands-on.

name: If on a Winter's Night a Traveller
description:
This edition of Co-Read will explore excerpts from Italo Calvino’s novel, *If on a Winter’s Night a Traveller*.

Join us to discover what happens when a book speaks to you directly, makes you its main character, only to interrupt every story as it begins. We will read short passages aloud and pass “you” around the circle, to piece together the many ways a book can involve its readers: as the author, an observer or a participant.

No prior knowledge of the book required.

name: Through the Looking Glass: From Molecules to Life
description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to researchers Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai for their work in asymmetric organic synthesis.

Life is built from molecules, yet living systems exhibit a remarkable preference for one molecular handedness over its mirror image. How did this asymmetry emerge, and how did it become embedded in the chemistry of life? 

Join Sankaranarayanan Rajan for a lecture exploring the fascinating interface between chemistry and biology, tracing the connections between molecular chirality, the origins of life, and the evolution of biological systems. Drawing on insights from Nobel Prize-winning discoveries in chemistry and contemporary research, he will examine how nature achieves molecular selectivity and fidelity through mechanisms that distinguish between seemingly similar molecular alternatives. The lecture will offer a glimpse into the fundamental principles that underpin life's molecular organisation.

This lecture is organised in collaboration with Infosys Science Foundation.

name: Back to School: We Make the Rules
description:
What if science didn't have to fit neatly into physics, chemistry, and biology? What if you could rewrite the textbook and decide how science should be explored?

This Children's Day, we're going back to school, but this time, you get to write the textbook! In this hands-on workshop, we'll explore surprising connections between things that seem completely unrelated, from everyday experiences to the world of quantum physics. You'll create your own science textbook filled with curious questions, fun experiments, unexpected facts, and a little imagination.

name: Macroeconomic Stabilisation
description:
The 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences went to researchers Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for their research on microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.

Join Chetan Ghate for a lecture reviewing the body of work by the laureates that led to them being awarded the prize in this area. The discussion will explore the relevance of their work in macroeconomic policy making as well as its importance in shaping macroeconomic policy frameworks for India. Be sure to attend this insightful session to learn more and to ask Chetan questions about his own work.

name: The Quantum Art Experiment
description:
What happens when quantum physics meets doodles, wild ideas, and a little bit of creative chaos?

Come find out! Join Divya Chalapathi for a session on mixing art and quantum curiosity through playful drawing experiments, unexpected twists, geometric patterns, and imaginative creations. Explore chance, possibilities, and connections as you create, exchange ideas, and let your imagination run wild. 

No drawing skills or quantum knowledge needed—just bring your curiosity! And the best part? You'll leave with your very own artwork to take home.
